guidelines.title: Single responsibility
guidelines.description: Keep work that changes for the same reason together.
guidelines.applicability: Review an observed boundary between different kinds of work.
guidelines.limitations: A small cohesive module can appropriately perform several steps of one workflow.
trade_offs: Splitting too early increases navigation and coordination.

guidelines.title: Separation of concerns
guidelines.description: Separate transport, durable storage and domain decisions where they evolve independently.
guidelines.limitations: A cross-boundary dependency is legitimate when ownership and direction are clear.
trade_offs: Extra layers introduce handoffs and mapping code.

guidelines.title: Dependency inversion
guidelines.description: Let business behavior depend on a narrow abstraction when infrastructure needs to vary.
guidelines.applicability: Review a domain-to-infrastructure dependency or an explicit need for substitutions.
guidelines.limitations: A stable concrete dependency can remain direct when there is no useful seam.
benefits: Infrastructure can be substituted in tests.
trade_offs: Interfaces and wiring add maintenance work.

guidelines.title: Loose coupling and high cohesion
guidelines.description: Keep closely related behavior together and keep shared dependencies narrow.
guidelines.applicability: Review a highly shared dependency or a domain infrastructure seam.
guidelines.limitations: A stable, cohesive shared module may be appropriate.
benefits: Limits the scope of coordinated changes.
trade_offs: Moving behavior can add adapters or duplicate small routines.

guidelines.title: Avoid circular dependencies
guidelines.description: Review observed directed cycles and consider a clearer dependency direction.
guidelines.applicability: A directed cycle exists in the observed dependency edges.
guidelines.limitations: Static relationships may be conditional. The reference describes Spring Modulith rules, which are advisory here unless explicitly configured as policy.

source.title: Spring Modulith · Verifying application module structure

trade_offs: Breaking a legitimate cycle can require moving responsibilities or introducing a boundary.

guidelines.title: Authorization boundaries
guidelines.description: Enforce access decisions at a trusted boundary for the relevant operation and resource.
guidelines.applicability: Source shows authorization or tenant handling, or requirements identify a protected boundary.
guidelines.limitations: Static excerpts cannot prove route coverage or policy effectiveness. Authentication and authorization have distinct responsibilities.
benefits: Makes access enforcement consistent and reviewable.
trade_offs: Shared checks require clear ownership and coverage tests.

guidelines.title: Configuration management
guidelines.description: Keep deployment-specific configuration separate from application behavior.
guidelines.applicability: Source shows environment-driven configuration or requirements identify deployment variation.
guidelines.limitations: Application constants may stay in code. Use an appropriate secret store for sensitive values.
benefits: Supports deployment variation without code changes.
trade_offs: Adds configuration validation and operational setup.

guidelines.title: Keep architecture simple
guidelines.description: Use the smallest design that addresses the demonstrated needs.
guidelines.applicability: The selected graph is small or simplicity is an explicit requirement.
guidelines.limitations: A bounded graph does not establish repository size. Separate boundaries can still be justified by ownership, risk, or deployment needs.

source.title: Microsoft Learn · Common web application architectures

trade_offs: A simple structure may need adjustment when requirements change.

guidelines.title: Maintainability and testability
guidelines.description: Expose useful seams for testing behavior with costly or variable dependencies.
guidelines.applicability: A test seam is observable or testability is requested.
guidelines.limitations: Static source cannot establish the quality or coverage of existing tests.
benefits: Supports focused tests for business behavior.
trade_offs: Test seams require maintenance and do not replace integration tests.

guidelines.title: FastAPI router boundaries
guidelines.description: Use routers and dependencies when groups of endpoints need distinct organization or shared setup.
guidelines.applicability: FastAPI imports are visible in the selected source evidence.
guidelines.limitations: Small FastAPI applications may remain in one module. Routers alone do not establish authorization coverage.
benefits: Makes related routes and shared dependencies easier to review.
trade_offs: Additional modules can add wiring and navigation.

guidelines.title: Spring Boot package boundaries
guidelines.description: Organize application packages so component discovery and domain ownership remain clear.
guidelines.applicability: Spring Boot imports or its application annotation appear in selected source.
guidelines.limitations: Spring Boot does not prescribe a fixed number of layers or a single package layout.
benefits: Makes component discovery and package ownership easier to inspect.
trade_offs: Package reorganization can require import and configuration changes.
